judgements.justification: Each committee raised checkable issues the other missed (A: memorization vs guidance scale, latent-space editing; B: boastful title, FID-guidance interaction, latency), so they weighed different problem sets, though no tier changed.
Stage 1 finds the same facts weighted the same way; shared weaknesses (novelty, sampling speed) were revision items in both committees.
Reviews were unanimous accepts in both committees; no split for an AC to resolve by adopting one reviewer.
The only score change (H51k, 6 to 7) came from the authors' novelty reply and model-release promise, not from the other reviews.
The authors answered every reviewer's substantive point; the unanswered title complaint did not affect jJSL's score by jJSL's own statement.
A's Fjfm gave a praise-only 9 at confidence 5 and ignored the rebuttal; B's yLx5 gave a thin 6 and did not reply; both scores counted unchallenged.
Both ACs gave a spotlight, in line with unanimous accept scores.
Neither meta-review invokes a score threshold; both restate the consensus.
No below-threshold score exists; yLx5's 6 is an accept rating on the central novelty point.
Both committees judged the paper as a generative-modelling methods advance with state-of-the-art results.
H51k raised at confidence 4 on a novelty argument within reach; no reviewer disclaimed expertise in the core.
Both committees applied the same bar: strong empirical results outweigh limited novelty.
The one wrong factual claim (yLx5 on architecture gains) lowered a score; no praise rests on a wrong claim.
yLx5 never acknowledged the rebuttal; H51k raised the score after the concern was answered.
Neither committee refused promised revisions; both treated remaining items as revision requests.
NtJ2's post-rebuttal 'I recommend an acceptance' matches the 7 it kept; no stated stance diverged from a score.
No extra reviewer was called in by either AC.
All reviewers in both committees found the paper clear; no clarity penalty tied to expertise.
H51k's raise came with a stated reason; no silent raise.
B's AC did not discount yLx5's rating; it simply restated the unanimous accept.
Each committee has a 9; A's is thin but A is not without a reviewer rating it that high.
No reviewer admitted reading only part of the paper.
No reviewer contested the premise from another theoretical tradition.
Both committees chose the same spotlight tier with consensus-only meta-reviews, so no tier gap rests on an unstated case.
Both committees knew the GAN and diffusion baselines; H51k and i9rh both checked against prior results.
Both meta-reviews describe the unanimous accept positions accurately.
No reviewer or AC raised a narrow-audience concern.
No misreading detractor pulled either AC to argue only acceptance; both reached spotlight.
The authors posted no new experiments to one forum only; the one-sided replies were statements (washed-out images, 300x speed gap), not results that moved scores.
No AC overrode a lone expert review with lower-confidence scores; tiers match.
No objection was added after the response period closed.
Means are equal at 7.5; Fjfm's inflated 9 is a single-reviewer outlier, not a committee-wide scale difference.
B's reviewers (jJSL, i9rh) and AC judged the title overstated and the AC required a new title, while A took the title at face value; the tier was not lowered.
No committee converged on marginal-accept scores at low confidence; A's 7s are at confidence 4 and the tier was spotlight.
